1_JYfF6gkcuh3YOffuBRyjMXJKMRj1w0N.text:
## Ad Liska
Born: July 10, 1906 · Died: Nov 30, 1998 · Class of 1925
PCL Baseball Hall of Fame · Oregon Sports Hall of Fame

Liska was the first Nebraska baseball player to make it to the big leagues. He started as a teacher and semi-pro player, even making an appearance at the age of 19 for the Lincoln Links in 1926. His big league debut came for the Washington Senators in 1929. After five years of major league service, he bounced around and found another stop in Nebraska with the Omaha Packers in 1935.

The signing that would define his career came with the Portland Beavers AA team in 1936. He dominated the PCL circuit for the rest of his career, pitching for the Beavers from age 29 to 42, amassing 242 minor league wins with a 3.05 ERA.

Former player Dario Lodigiani, who faced Liska while Ad was in his 40s, said "I was so bad against Liska (in the PCL) that I think even if he had walked the ball up to the plate, I couldn't have hit him."

The enclosed cut signature came from the pictured PSA/DNA certified index card, bearing certification number L14850.
